Standard: Emergency exits are assessed IAW the following: a. Each occupied compartment has at least one emergency egress exit, and areas with seating restraints have emergency egress exits to the exterior of the air vehicle. b. Exits are operable from inside and outside the compartments for interior doors, and from inside and outside the air vehicle for exterior exits. c. Emergency egress exits are located away from hazardous areas of the air vehicle (e.g., propellers, or jet engine inlets and outlets) while still meeting egress time IAW the timed egress criteria. d. Emergency exits are not located in areas that will be blocked after an emergency gear up landing (e.g., doors can be opened and closed with landing gear up and locked). e. Emergency exits are large enough to allow the full range of anthropometric sizes and worst-case mission equipment (if applicable) to egress within the time allowed IAW 9.6.3.5, 9.6.3.6, 9.6.3.7, or 9.6.3.8. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of engineering drawings, digital models, or high-fidelity mockups verifies that each occupied compartment has an exit.
(2) Examination of engineering drawings, digital models, or high-fidelity mockups verifies that doors are operable IAW the standard.
(3) Examination of engineering drawings, digital models, or high-fidelity mockups verifies that exit locations are outside of documented hazardous areas (e.g., keep-out zones around engines or propellers) of the air vehicle.
(4) Examination of engineering drawings, digital models, or high-fidelity mockups show that emergency exits can be operated with the landing gear up. Demonstration.
  (1) Demonstrate egress times IAW 9.6.3.5, 9.6.3.6, 9.6.3.7, or 9.6.3.8.
